identity.industry: Industrials / Contract Sheet-Metal & Heavy Fabrication (laser-cutting, bending, welding, machining job-work for OEMs)

summary.oneLiner: Rishi Laser is a small (~INR 160 cr) contract heavy-fabrication job-worker that just spent a painful FY26 commissioning a new Caterpillar-dedicated Malur plant — management took unusually candid full ownership of a self-inflicted execution miss (PAT -55% to INR 3.67 cr on commissioning drag + a doubled employee cost from running old and new plants in parallel). The investment cost is now "behind us": Malur is live (targeting INR 60 cr FY27 → INR 100 cr by FY29) with a Phase-1 in-house paint shop, and the bet is that operating leverage on a maintained ~49% gross margin converts to higher EBITDA from FY27. The bull case rides on Caterpillar's global ramp + China+1 export sourcing; the bear case (pressed hard by holders on the call) is six sub-scale plants, chronic ~10% EBITDA despite 50% gross margin, and a 30% Karnataka minimum-wage hike.

financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > One-offs (non-recurring per mgmt): Malur ramp-up costs, restructuring/duplication of employee cost, commissioning drag — all in the FY26 P&L, "will not repeat in FY27 at the same scale."
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Revenue: ~20% (mgmt also says 20–25%) company revenue CAGR over next 3 yrs → implies ~INR 285–300 cr by ~FY29. Malur INR 60 cr FY27 (but ~INR 25–30 cr of the existing INR 160 cr base shifts INTO Malur, so not additive). Net company FY27 ~INR 190 cr (analysts pushed for INR 210–225 cr).
Malur ramp: INR 60 cr FY27 → INR 100 cr by FY29 (maybe earlier); all product approvals in place, billing/shipments to Caterpillar already started.
Margin: FY27 EBITDA band 9–11% (mgmt non-committal on a path to 13–15%; agreed double-digit is the aspiration but would not commit).
Caterpillar growth: +15–20% at least in FY27; upside if larger new items click + entry into Caterpillar global supply chain + Perkins/engine division.
Pune plant: target ~INR 50 cr FY27 (from ~INR 36 cr), ~80% utilization, possibly full by Q3FY27. Vadodara flat (key customer down).
Robotics/automation: FY26 ~INR 2 cr; FY27 target INR 5 cr, possibly revised to INR 10 cr if pipeline (up 300–400% since March) converts.
Capex left: Phase-2 paint shop ~INR 2–3 cr pending; otherwise plant fully capitalized.
order book & pipeline: No formal order book disclosed (job-work model). Visibility is customer-relationship-driven.
Caterpillar (largest client, Malur-dedicated): "very positive and very promising," all verticals guiding a good ramp for at least first 6 months of FY27.
New early-stage export construction-equipment customers: 2–3 major MNCs in trials; trial orders received last month; could contribute from Q3FY27 (not in the INR 40–50 cr Pune figure).
New construction-industry opportunity: scaffolding + aluminium formwork (metal forming for cement pouring) — some new orders won.
segment / subsidiary detail: Construction-equipment fabrication (~53% of rev): core growth engine; Caterpillar is #1 client. Malur built for medium & heavy fabrication for this segment; large/complex assemblies.

Electrical / power switchgear enclosures: customers Schneider (#1 here, but offtake fell drastically since Q4 last year — medium-voltage switchgear, no explanation given), ABB, Siemens (smaller). Mgmt explicit: the power/transformer boom is NOT flowing to Rishi because it supplies the wrong (non-booming) sub-segment.
Industrial/process: Emerson, Volvo (scaling), other exporters — feeding Pune plant traction.
Robotics & automation systems: moving from SME work toward complex automation for construction-equipment & auto tier-1 customers (better margin); inflection expected FY27.
Plants: Malur (new, live), old Bangalore/Bommasandra (capacity shifting to Malur), Pune (export-focused, ramping to ~80%), Vadodara (flat; first US export order just won).
growth verticals / optionality: Caterpillar global supply chain + Perkins/engine division: the big optionality — Caterpillar's engine division (data-center / power-generation driven) is its fastest-growing globally; Perkins plant Aurangabad + Hosur; Rishi getting first inquiries from a division it did "no work" for till last year.

Exports / China+1: Western OEM costs "haywire," overseas players seeking India sourcing; export margins ~3–5 ppt above domestic (freight a partial offset). Long-cycle global earthmoving boom = the lever to scale beyond INR 300 cr.
Robotics/automation business: pipeline up 300–400%; potential "spectacular" 5-yr growth, partly riding manpower-shortage tailwind at large OEMs/tier-1s.
Scaffolding & aluminium formwork for the construction boom.
Tubes business: shelved for ~12 months (bandwidth); only the welding side started, forming deferred.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin ~49% and stable (the structural strength); EBITDA stuck ~8.7% — the gap is overhead spread across six plants + the FY26 cost spike.

Employee cost is the #1 challenge: doubled to ~INR 33 cr partly on old+new plant duplication (non-recurring) but structurally pressured by Karnataka's proposed ~30% minimum-wage hike. Mitigation = automation/robotics (5–6 robots installed, +8–10 more in FY27) + smoother workflow (idle skilled labour is non-fungible across cells).
Raw-material pass-through: quarterly mechanism for most customers; passes through if RM moves >±5%, with ~one-quarter lag.
Finance cost: expected flat to Q4 run-rate, gradually down as cash flows repay debt.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Major capex cycle effectively complete: total assets INR 148.7 cr, PPE INR 94.7 cr, D/E 0.29x.
Remaining: Phase-2 paint shop ~INR 2–3 cr. Phase-1 paint shop went live Jun-26 (new capability improving value proposition + margin on finished assemblies).
Risk flagged by holders: continuously adding plants/paint-shop spend at a sub-scale revenue base without consolidating idle facilities → capital-efficiency concern.
capital allocation: Disciplined balance sheet (D/E 0.29x; "very good" fixed-asset-to-turnover ratio; capacity built at low cost vs peers).
Heavy reinvestment phase just ended; FY27 framed as the year to convert capex into revenue/margin.

Shareholder pushback on capital efficiency: multiple long-term holders (one ~3.5–4% holder) pressed for plant consolidation and a credible path to 13–14% EBITDA; mgmt conceded the point but offered no consolidation plan.
risks & watch-items: Execution credibility: missed FY26 guidance badly; conservative-on-purpose FY27 guidance (INR 190 cr) vs analyst-implied INR 210–225 cr — watch whether they sandbag or under-deliver again.
Margin stuck ~10% despite ~49% gross margin — six sub-scale plants, no consolidation plan; the core debate.
Employee cost / Karnataka +30% minimum wage — structural cost headwind.
Customer concentration: Caterpillar is the dominant client and Malur is largely dedicated to it; Schneider (top electrical client) offtake collapsed unexplained since Q4 last year.
Power-sector boom is a non-event for Rishi — it supplies the wrong switchgear sub-segment; do not model the transformer/T&D upcycle into this name.
Vadodara flat (major customer down); idle capacity risk if utilization doesn't lift.
Geopolitical / RM price volatility (steel) cited as reason for conservative guidance.
management quality / tone: Strikingly candid: opening statement (read by CFO on behalf of the MD) explicitly owned "two execution, two leadership failures" (capital execution + human-capital readiness) without hedging — multiple analysts praised the honesty. MD Harshad Patel engaged seriously with hard capital-allocation pushback (Viraj Mehta, Manoj Dua) and agreed that failing to reach double-digit EBITDA "I would also treat as a failure." Tone is humble, realistic, slightly conservative ("earn it back through results, not promises") but lacking a hard, quantified margin-bridge — which holders flagged as the gap between commentary and numbers.
non-obvious takeaways: The headline INR 160 cr → INR 190 cr FY27 step is largely the INR 25–30 cr Bangalore→Malur internal shift, not net new growth — the "INR 60 cr Malur" is partly cannibalisation; real organic growth is smaller than the optics.

The transformer/grid-capex boom does NOT benefit Rishi (top electrical client Schneider's medium-voltage switchgear offtake actually fell) — a useful corrective for anyone tagging it a "power capex" supplier.

The genuine optionality is Caterpillar's engine/Perkins division (data-center & power-gen driven globally) and getting into Caterpillar's global supply chain — currently near-zero revenue, but the only path management sees beyond INR 300 cr.
Automation/robotics is both a product line (target INR 5–10 cr) and the defensive answer to a 30% wage hike — watch the robot install count (5–6 → +8–10).
This is a deep-value / execution-turnaround micro-cap (mcap ~INR 117 cr, ~92 lakh shares): the entire thesis hinges on FY27 operating leverage actually showing up after a year of broken promises.

qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q4 FY26 (this): FY26 revenue INR 160 cr (+7%, missed target); PAT INR 3.67 cr (-55%); EBITDA margin 8.7% (vs 9.1%); gross margin ~49% (maintained); exports INR 22.83 cr (14.2%); employee cost ~INR 33 cr (doubled, partly one-off); Malur plant + Phase-1 paint shop now live; D/E 0.29x. Guidance: FY27 ~INR 190 cr (analysts pushed 210–225), Malur INR 60 cr, EBITDA 9–11%, Caterpillar +15–20%, Pune ~INR 50 cr.

Next Q → check: (1) FY27 revenue tracking to INR 190 cr (or the bull INR 220 cr); (2) does Malur actually bill ~INR 60 cr; (3) EBITDA margin lifting toward 11%+ (operating leverage proof); (4) employee cost % of sales down off the FY26 aberration despite Karnataka wage hike; (5) Pune utilization to ~80%/INR 50 cr; (6) Caterpillar Perkins/engine + global supply-chain orders; (7) robotics revenue INR 5→10 cr; (8) Schneider switchgear offtake recovery; (9) any plant consolidation move.

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).
